title: Behavioral contract fuzz + healing shim for OpenAI Responses migrations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers migrating from OpenAI Responses to Redwood's Responses-compatible endpoint observe sporadic behavioral deltas across streaming events, tool/function call boundaries, and structured-output framing. These deltas include out-of-order event fragments, missing deterministic toolcall start/end markers, truncated structured JSON blocks across stream chunk boundaries, and token-provenance mismatches that break downstream parsers and retrievers.

Goal: Build a lightweight, runtime-capable "healing shim" and accompanying fuzz-and-observability pipeline that: 1) discovers and catalogs real-world event/sequence deltas via fuzzing and production sampling, 2) provides deterministic canonicalization rules (strict/permissive modes) to repair streaming fragments and reconstitute structured outputs, and 3) ships a canaryable runtime flag and safety fallback that preserves caller semantics with minimal latency impact.

Scope: Engineering ticket covers the fuzz harness, a library of canonicalizers (stream-reassemble, functioncall delimiter reconciliation, structured-output stitcher), runtime integration hooks for Redwood serving runtime, telemetry events and SLO guardrails, and the canary rollout plan. This ticket does not include SDK surface changes; if needed we will open a follow-up PM ticket to coordinate API docs and SDK shims.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzz harness that replays 10k synthetic and 2k sampled production traces producing a categorized delta catalogue (stream reorder, missing markers, truncated JSON, inconsistent toolcall signature)
Canonicalizer library implemented with two modes: permissive (best-effort reassembly) and strict (reject + clear error), exposed as a runtime flag
End-to-end microbenchmark showing <5ms median added latency for permissive shim under 50 concurrent requests
Telemetry events for every healed trace with tags: delta_type, severity, canonicalizer_mode, request_id; dashboards in Console showing healed rate over time
Canary rollout runbook and automated rollback if healed_rate > 2% and customer_error_rate increases > 0.5% in canary cohort
Comprehensive unit/integration tests and a public canary-run log for one week with zero high-severity incidents
implementation_notes: Fuzz harness: leverage responses-proxy recorder to capture streaming frames, then mutate chunk boundaries and event order to surface edge cases
Canonicalizers: implement three pluggable transforms: chunk-stitcher, toolcall-boundedizer, structured-json-reassembler
Use sequence numbers and lightweight reassembly buffer with a configurable byte/timeout threshold to avoid head-of-line blocking
Expose runtime flag: 'resp_compat_mode' with values ['off','permissive','strict'] and a per-route override in routing policies
Instrument with coarse sampling in prod (0.1%) and full tracing for canary routes
Benchmarking harness uses qps profiles from real tenant traces to measure latency tail impact and memory footprint
test_plan: Unit tests for each canonicalizer covering 200+ synthesized cases (fragmented JSON, nested functioncall tokens crossing chunks, missing close markers)
Integration tests that replay mutated production traces and assert consumer-visible schema invariants (valid JSON, consistent toolcall start/end pairing)
Load tests at 10x baseline QPS to validate latency and memory behavior under permissive mode
Chaos test injecting duplicate/rewritten events to validate idempotency and no-client-visible duplication
Canary tests with 5% traffic for 7 days capturing healed_rate, error_rate, latency_p95 and customer-facing SDK logs
rollout_plan: Dev deploy: library behind feature-flag; run fuzz harness and generate delta catalogue (this ticket)
Staging: enable 'permissive' mode on staging; run integration suites against SDK consumer harness
Canary: enable permissive on 5% of production routes with full telemetry and automated rollback thresholds
Observe for 7 days; if healed_rate stabilizes and no latency uplift beyond guardrails, expand to 30% then 100%
Post-rollout: evaluate adoption of 'strict' mode for opt-in customers and document migration guidance
